auth.description: HubSpot private-app access token (pat-…) with crm.objects.contacts.read/write, crm.objects.companies.read and crm.objects.deals.read
auth.name: hubspot.access_token
auth.subject: unstated

description: HubSpot CRM: read contacts, companies and deals, and create and update contact records

contract.description: Read one contact by record id. Returns only HubSpot's default contact properties — name, email and record timestamps; a custom property needs a `properties` projection this connector cannot express yet. A non-2xx response is returned as data, not a failure: the vendor's error message is at `/message`, its error code at `/category` in the response body.

operations.description: Read one contact by record id. Returns only HubSpot's default contact properties — name, email and record timestamps; a custom property needs a `properties` projection this connector cannot express yet

params.description: The contact's HubSpot record id (`hs_object_id`), e.g. 512
params.name: contact_id

archived.description: True for a record in the recycle bin

archivedAt.description: Present only on an archived record

associations.description: Related records — companies, deals, tickets — keyed by object type. Returned only when asked for. Present on this read schema and absent from the create's

createdAt.description: When the record was created — an ISO timestamp here, unlike the epoch-milliseconds string the equivalent `createdate` property carries

id.description: The record id (`hs_object_id`) **as a string**, even though this operation takes it as a number

properties.description: The contact's property values, keyed by HubSpot's internal property name (`email`, `firstname`, `lastname`, `createdate`, `lastmodifieddate`, `hs_object_id`). EVERY VALUE IS A STRING regardless of the property's configured type — a number is `"17"`, a checkbox `"false"`, a date the epoch-milliseconds string `"1572480000000"`. Which keys are present depends on the portal's own property set and on the `properties` projection this connector cannot send

propertiesWithHistory.description: Previous values per property, each an array of `{value, timestamp, sourceType}`. Returned only when asked for, which this connector cannot do

contract.description: Create a contact from an email address. HubSpot treats email as the contact's unique identifier and rejects a duplicate with 409. The new record is visible to everyone in the portal and can be enrolled by a workflow, which may send it marketing email. A non-2xx response is returned as data, not a failure: the vendor's error message is at `/message`, its error code at `/category` in the response body.

operations.description: Create a contact from an email address. HubSpot treats email as the contact's unique identifier and rejects a duplicate with 409. The new record is visible to everyone in the portal and can be enrolled by a workflow, which may send it marketing email

params.description: The contact's email address — HubSpot's unique identifier for a contact
params.name: email

id.description: The new record's id, as a string. This is the `contact_id` for a following update — and the update's parameter is a number, so it has to be converted

properties.description: The created record's properties, keyed by internal name, EVERY VALUE A STRING. HubSpot fills in more than was sent — `createdate`, `lastmodifieddate` and `hs_object_id` at minimum

warnings.description: Non-fatal complaints about the create — a property HubSpot ignored, for instance. Present only on the create schema, and worth reading: the call still succeeded

contract.description: Overwrite a contact's first and last name. Both are written on every call — this operation replaces them rather than merging, so re-send the one you are not changing (read it first with hubspot-contact-get). The change is visible to everyone in the portal and can trigger a workflow. A non-2xx response is returned as data, not a failure: the vendor's error message is at `/message`, its error code at `/category` in the response body.

operations.description: Overwrite a contact's first and last name. Both are written on every call — this operation replaces them rather than merging, so re-send the one you are not changing (read it first with hubspot-contact-get). The change is visible to everyone in the portal and can trigger a workflow

params.description: The contact's first name; written on every call
params.name: firstname

params.description: The contact's last name; written on every call
params.name: lastname

contract.description: Read one company by record id. Returns only HubSpot's default company properties — name, domain and record timestamps. A non-2xx response is returned as data, not a failure: the vendor's error message is at `/message`, its error code at `/category` in the response body.

operations.description: Read one company by record id. Returns only HubSpot's default company properties — name, domain and record timestamps

associations.description: Related contacts, deals and tickets. Returned only when asked for

id.description: The company's record id, as a string

properties.description: The company's property values, keyed by internal name (`name`, `domain`, `createdate`, `hs_lastmodifieddate`, `hs_object_id`). EVERY VALUE IS A STRING — including numeric properties such as `numberofemployees` and `annualrevenue`

propertiesWithHistory.description: Returned only when asked for, which this connector cannot do

contract.description: Read one deal by record id. Returns only HubSpot's default deal properties — name, amount, stage, pipeline and close date. A non-2xx response is returned as data, not a failure: the vendor's error message is at `/message`, its error code at `/category` in the response body.

operations.description: Read one deal by record id. Returns only HubSpot's default deal properties — name, amount, stage, pipeline and close date

associations.description: The contacts and companies on the deal. Returned only when asked for

id.description: The deal's record id, as a string

properties.description: The deal's property values, keyed by internal name (`dealname`, `amount`, `dealstage`, `pipeline`, `closedate`, `hs_object_id`). EVERY VALUE IS A STRING — `amount` arrives as `"1500.00"` and `closedate` as an ISO string, so a numeric or date comparison has to convert first. `dealstage` and `pipeline` are per-portal internal ids, not display names
